text.p: Israeli warplanes hit Hizbollah targets in a south Lebanon area for the third consecutive day on Sunday, Lebanese security sources said.
Two Israeli fighter jets fired two rockets into the hills of Jabal ad-Dahr Daidaba southwest of the Bekaa Valley, where Hizbollah guerrillas killed three Israeli soldiers on Thursday, they said.
There was no immediate word on casualties in the air raid -- the fifth into Lebanon in three days and the 35th in 1997.
Simultaneously, Israeli artillerymen rocketed the area and a pilotless reconnaissance aircraft was seen in the air.
Shortly after the air raid, Hizbollah said its guerrillas fired mortar bombs into the Israeli outpost of Kawkaba just inside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.
There was no immediate confirmation of the attack from inside the zone.
On Thursday, the guerrillas killed three Israeli soldiers and wounded seven when clashes erupted with a group of Israeli commandos 2 km (one mile) north of the zone.
The attack brought to nine the number of Israeli soldiers killed and to 35 the number of wounded in guerrilla attacks since the beginning of the year.
Two Hizbollah guerrillas were killed in the fighting.
The pro-Iranian guerrillas attack Israeli troops and their local militia allies in a bid to oust them from the 15-km (nine miles)-wide occupation zone.
